title: Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen (SAW)? How to Choose and Get to Your Hotel
excerpt: Pick your Istanbul arrival airport by where you sleep, when you land and where you go next, then compare the M11, M4, Havaist, Havabüs and İETT options from each terminal.

body.text: Istanbul has two big passenger airports on opposite sides of the Bosphorus: Istanbul Airport (IST) on the European side and Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) on the Asian side. Flight search results mix them under one city name, so the cheapest ticket can quietly add a long cross-city journey to your first evening. This guide gives you a decision framework rather than a single answer: start with where you are sleeping, then check arrival time, luggage and your next connection, and only then compare fares.
The quick answer: start from your bed for the night

items: Staying on the Asian side (Kadıköy, Üsküdar, Moda, Bostancı) or in Pendik: SAW is usually the natural choice. The M4 metro runs between Kadıköy and Sabiha Gökçen, and Havabüs and several İETT buses also link the airport with Kadıköy.

Staying around Levent, Gayrettepe, Şişli or the northern business districts: IST is usually simpler. The M11 metro starts at Gayrettepe, and Havaist and İETT buses serve Mecidiyeköy, 4. Levent and Taksim.

Staying in the old city (Sultanahmet, Eminönü) or Beyoğlu/Taksim: both can work. IST has direct Havaist lines to Sultanahmet and Taksim; from SAW you can ride the Havabüs to Taksim or go via Kadıköy and continue by ferry across the water.
Unsure where you will stay: book accommodation first, or at least choose the side of the city, before you commit to a flight.

body.text: On its Istanbul flights page, [Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-us/flights/flights-to-istanbul/) says its Istanbul flights operate from Istanbul Airport, while its AJet brand flies to Sabiha Gökçen. [Pegasus](https://www.flypgs.com/basin-bultenleri/metro-istanbul-ve-pegasus-hava-yollari-istasyon-isim-hakki-anlasmasina-imza-atti) describes Sabiha Gökçen as its home airport. Other carriers vary by route and season, so always check the three-letter airport code on the booking itself — ‘Istanbul (all airports)’ in a search box is not a destination. If two separate tickets land you at IST and leave from SAW (or the other way round), treat that as a cross-city transfer, not a connection.
What the 2026 traffic figures tell you

DHMİ, the state airports authority, publishes provisional passenger statistics. Its [January–July 2026 table](https://www.dhmi.gov.tr/Lists/Istatislikler/Attachments/439/YOLCU.pdf) lists 48,068,524 arriving and departing passengers for Istanbul Airport (about 2% up on the same period of 2025) and 28,014,566 for Sabiha Gökçen (about 6% up); the Transport Minister gave the same totals for the two airports when announcing the seven-month figures, as [reported by Hürriyet Daily News](https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiyes-airports-served-nearly-139-mln-passengers-in-first-seven-months-225439). The split is the useful part for travellers: roughly one in five IST passengers in that period flew domestically, compared with just under half at SAW, where domestic traffic grew 11%. In practice, SAW is a busy domestic gateway as well as an international one, which matters if you are combining Istanbul with Cappadocia, Antalya or Izmir. These are provisional figures and DHMİ notes they can be revised.
From Istanbul Airport (IST) to the city

The [airport’s transport page](https://www.istairport.com/en/airport/airport-transportation) lists three public options: the M11 metro, Havaist coaches and İETT city buses. Havaist and İETT board on transportation floor -2.

items: M11 metro: the airport describes it as 15 stops from Gayrettepe to Halkalı, with the Halkalı–Arnavutköy section opened on 20 June 2026. The same page points to TCDD’s website for further line information. Gayrettepe is the useful end for Levent, Şişli and onward metro connections. Check the line’s status and operating hours for your travel date before you fly.

Havaist coaches: [Havaist’s stops page](https://www.hava.ist/duraklar.php) lists lines including Sultanahmet (HVL-13), Taksim and Taksim Express (HVL-9), Aksaray Metro (HVL-1), Kadıköy (HVL-6), Bakırköy, Halkalı, Esenler bus terminal and Sabiha Gökçen (HVİST-13). The same page says credit cards are accepted on its buses.

İETT buses: [İETT’s airport page](https://iett.istanbul/icerik/Access-to-Airports) lists H-1 (Mahmutbey Metro), H-2 (Mecidiyeköy), H-3 (Halkalı), H-6 (Arnavutköy) and H-8 (Hacıosman/Sarıyer) among its IST lines.

Fares: Havaist’s own July 2026 article on the Sultanahmet line shows two different figures (8 euros in the text, a lira amount in the page summary). We do not quote a fare here; check the price in the operator’s ticket channel on the day.

body.text: From Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) to the city

items: M4 metro: the line is named M4 Kadıköy–Sabiha Gökçen Havalimanı, with its last station at the airport (the station carries Pegasus naming rights under a three-year agreement announced in 2024). Ayrılık Çeşmesi on the M4 is a transfer to Marmaray, according to the [M4 line overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M4_(Istanbul_Metro)), which helps if you are heading under the Bosphorus to the European side.

Havabüs: the [airport’s Havabüs page](https://www.sabihagokcen.aero/havabus-en) says white Havabüs shuttles wait in front of the terminal exits on the arrivals floor and run to Kadıköy (the pier) and Taksim (last stop at the Divan Hotel).

İETT buses: İETT lists SAW lines including E-3 (4. Levent Metro), E-9 (Bostancı), E-10 and E-11 and SG-1 (Kadıköy), SG-2 (Taksim), 122H (Yenişehir–4. Levent), 16S (Uzunçayır Metrobus) and 132H (Pendik YHT).

Old city via the water: the airport suggests reaching Kadıköy and then taking a ferry to Eminönü before walking or taking the tram to Sultanahmet. It also says İETT buses and ferries need an Istanbulkart, sold at İETT kiosks near the bus waiting area. For how ferries and transfers work in town, see our [Istanbul public transport guide](/blog/istanbul-public-transport-tourist-guide).

body.text: Late arrivals, heavy bags and taxis

We do not list first and last departures here, because none of the official pages we opened gave timetables that we could confirm for your travel date. If you land late, look up the last metro, Havaist or Havabüs departure for your exact day on the operator’s channel before you book, and have a fallback. With large suitcases or children, a single direct coach or taxi can be worth more than a cheaper multi-change route: metro transfers mean stairs, crowds and platform walks. The Sabiha Gökçen page notes that taxis wait in front of the terminal at arrivals level; at either airport, use the official rank, keep your address written in Turkish and confirm the fare method before you set off. A pre-booked private transfer is another option some travellers choose; compare it on the same door-to-door basis.
If you are travelling on within Türkiye

items: Domestic flight next: check which Istanbul airport your onward flight uses before booking the inbound one. Havaist’s HVİST-13 runs between the two airports, but that is a long road trip, not a terminal walk; plan an overnight stay if the gap is tight.

High-speed train to Ankara or Konya: İETT’s 132H links SAW with Pendik YHT station, and the M11 ends at Halkalı. Our [Istanbul–Ankara YHT booking checklist](/blog/istanbul-ankara-yht-booking-checklist) explains how to check which Istanbul station your train actually uses.
Multi-day trip: if you are still shaping the route, our [3, 5 and 7-day Istanbul itinerary](/blog/istanbul-itinerary-3-5-7-days) helps you decide which side of the city to base yourself on.

body.text: Price check: compare the whole journey

Put each option in one row: flight fare, checked-bag fee, transfer cost for everyone in your group, transfer time and the arrival hour. A cheaper SAW flight for a Taksim hotel, or a cheaper IST flight for a Kadıköy flat, can lose its advantage once you add a cross-city coach or taxi and an extra hour. The reverse also happens: a slightly dearer ticket into the ‘right’ airport often buys you an earlier dinner.

items: Confirm the airport code (IST or SAW) on both your inbound and outbound tickets.
Match it to your accommodation’s side of the city and nearest metro, Havaist, Havabüs or İETT stop.
Check the last public-transport departure for your arrival date and a taxi fallback.
Check the current fare and accepted payment for the coach or bus you plan to use; carry an Istanbulkart for İETT buses and ferries.
Add buffers for onward domestic flights or trains, and never plan an IST–SAW connection as if it were the same airport.

seo.intent: Decide whether to fly into Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) and plan the public-transport or taxi transfer to the accommodation.
seo.uniqueValue: A stay-location-first decision framework for IST vs SAW that pairs airline bases and DHMİ January–July 2026 domestic/international splits with official M11, M4, Havaist, Havabüs and İETT line lists, plus onward YHT and domestic-flight checks; no unsourced fares or timetables.

quality.reviewNotes: Draft by a writer subagent; independent reviewer re-opened every source: DHMİ PDF row "İstanbul (*)" confirmed as Istanbul Airport via the minister's figures (HDN, Yeni Asır), Wikipedia-only M11 claims removed and the M11 Wikipedia source dropped, M4 Wikipedia source kept for one minor transfer claim, Havaist fare contradiction disclosed and no fare quoted; no hours, fares or journey times given. Translation review of DE, zh-CN, KO, ES: faithful, links verified. Editorial attestation, not native-speaker certification.
